title: IMMUNE DYSREGULATION WITH AUTOIMMUNITY, AUTOINFLAMMATION, AND IMMUNODEFICIENCY

relationships.phenotype: IMMUNE DYSREGULATION WITH AUTOIMMUNITY, AUTOINFLAMMATION, AND IMMUNODEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that susceptibility to severe invasive infections is caused by mutation in the IRAK2 gene (603304) on chromosome 3p25.3.

checks.claim: Susceptibility to severe invasive infections is caused by mutation in the IRAK2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: In two patients with sequential or repeated invasive infections: herpes simplex virus-triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with tuberculosis, and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia respectively, novel mutations of IRAK2 were identified.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports IRAK2 mutations in two patients with severe invasive infections. It also shows that the mutations impaired TRAF6 ubiquitination and TNF-alpha production, which supports a causal link. The paper's wording is more cautious ('linked', 'potential central role').

checks.claim: The IRAK2 gene is located on chromosome 3p25.3.
checks.evidence_quote: novel mutations of IRAK2 were identified
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state the chromosomal location. However, giving the gene's chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that restates the paper's gene identification, so the claim counts as supported.

paragraphs.text: Amali et al. (2024) reported 2 patients who had sequential or repeated invasive infections. In the first patient, herpes simplex virus infection triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), and the patient also had tuberculosis. The second patient had Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia.

checks.claim: Amali et al. (2024) reported 2 patients with IRAK2-related disease who had sequential or repeated invasive infections.
checks.evidence_quote: In two patients with sequential or repeated invasive infections: herpes simplex virus-triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with tuberculosis, and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia respectively, novel mutations of IRAK2 were identified.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that 2 patients with IRAK2 mutations had sequential or repeated invasive infections.

checks.claim: In the first IRAK2 patient reported by Amali et al. (2024), herpes simplex virus infection triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).
checks.evidence_quote: herpes simplex virus-triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with tuberculosis, and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia respectively
checks.explanation: Because of 'respectively', the first patient is the one with HSV-triggered HLH.

checks.claim: The first IRAK2 patient reported by Amali et al. (2024) also had tuberculosis.
checks.evidence_quote: herpes simplex virus-triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with tuberculosis
checks.explanation: The first patient had tuberculosis as well as HSV-triggered HLH.

checks.claim: The second IRAK2 patient reported by Amali et al. (2024) had Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia.
checks.evidence_quote: and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia respectively
checks.explanation: The second patient had S. pneumoniae bacteremia.

checks.claim: The second IRAK2 patient reported by Amali et al. (2024) had candidemia.
checks.evidence_quote: and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia respectively

paragraphs.text: Amali et al. (2024) identified novel mutations in the IRAK2 gene in 2 patients with sequential or repeated invasive infections (see CLINICAL FEATURES). The specific variants and their zygosity were not given in the evidence available. In functional studies, the IRAK2 variants impaired TRAF6 ubiquitination (or functional modification), which reduced TNF-alpha production. The authors proposed that IRAK2 may play a central role in host defense against a wide range of pathogens.

checks.claim: Amali et al. (2024) identified novel mutations in the IRAK2 gene in 2 patients with sequential or repeated invasive infections.
checks.evidence_quote: In two patients with sequential or repeated invasive infections: herpes simplex virus-triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with tuberculosis, and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia respectively, novel mutations of IRAK2 were identified.

checks.claim: In functional studies by Amali et al. (2024), the patients' IRAK2 variants impaired TRAF6 ubiquitination (or functional modification).
checks.evidence_quote: These mutations compromised the capacity to ubiquinate (or functionally modify) the signal adaptor tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 6.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the mutations impaired TRAF6 ubiquitination.

checks.claim: In functional studies by Amali et al. (2024), the patients' IRAK2 variants reduced TNF-alpha production.
checks.evidence_quote: The result is impairment of the cytokine tumor necrosis factor-alpha production.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that TNF-alpha production was impaired.

checks.claim: Amali et al. (2024) proposed that IRAK2 may play a central role in host defense against a wide range of pathogens.
checks.evidence_quote: This susceptibility to a varied range of pathogens underlines a potential central role played by IRAK2 in mediating host defense in infectious diseases.
checks.explanation: The draft accurately restates the authors' conclusion.
